title: Wrong Input, Wrong Threshold: Re-evaluating Adversarial Facial Privacy
abstract: arXiv:2611.21923v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Published face-privacy methods report protection above 90% against black-box recognition models. That number comes from an evaluation protocol with two independent defects, reported in a measure that cannot size either one. The input is wrong: methods published since 2022 feed the network the whole photograph, or a detector's box, where deployed systems detect, align to a landmark template and crop. Re-scoring the same files through a realistic front end costs a standard transfer attack 56% of its dodging protection and a budget-allocating attack 7%, with no image regenerated. The measure is wrong: that loss is a difference of success rates, so it saturates, moving by 8.2x over a budget sweep while the effect beneath it moves by 1.34x. We therefore report the paired cosine shift, in which both thresholds cancel algebraically, so the input defect holds without committing to a calibration. Measured that way it is 2.2x and 10.7x larger on

translated_title: 错误的输入，错误的阈值：重新评估对抗性面部隐私
translated_abstract: 已发表的面部隐私方法报告称，其对黑盒识别模型的保护率超过90%。然而这个数字来自一个存在两个独立缺陷的评估协议，并且所用度量无法衡量这两个缺陷中的任何一个。输入是错误的：2022年以来发表的方法将整张照片或检测器框直接输入网络，而实际部署的系统则会先进行人脸检测、对齐到关键点模板再裁剪。在不重新生成图像的情况下，仅通过现实的前端对相同文件重新评分，就会使标准迁移攻击失去56%的躲避保护，使预算分配攻击失去7%。度量也是错误的：这种损失是成功率的差值，因此会饱和——在预算扫描中该指标变化了8.2倍，而其背后的实际效应仅变化1.34倍。因此，我们报告配对余弦偏移，其中两个阈值在代数上相互抵消，使得输入缺陷的结论无需依赖任何校准即可成立。以这种方式测量，该效应分别大2.2倍和10.7倍于……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 论文揭示了现有对抗性面部隐私评估协议的两个独立缺陷——错误的输入方式（直接使用整图而非真实部署系统的检测、对齐、裁剪流程）和会饱和的成功率差值度量，并提出用配对余弦偏移这一新度量重新评估，发现现实前端会使标准迁移攻击的隐私保护效果损失56%。
en_tdlr: The paper identifies two independent flaws in current adversarial facial privacy evaluations—wrong inputs (whole photographs instead of the detect-align-crop pipeline of deployed systems) and a saturating success-rate-difference metric—and proposes the paired cosine shift as a calibration-free measure, showing that a realistic front end strips 56% of dodging protection from a standard transfer attack.
